notes.decision: Translated as 'face' (= πρόσωπον). Lycopolitan compound where ⲟⲉⲣ- is a pre-element on ϩⲟ ('face'). Appears throughout the chapter as the technical term for the four cosmic 'faces' of Light and Darkness — distinct entities/personae through which each principle manifests.
Rendered 'purpose-of-heart' per the established vocabulary (ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ from earlier pages). Here applied to the Greatness = the Father's intention/will which the four faces are sent to fulfill.

Translated 'to keep guard.' The form appears to be a Lycopolitan reduplication / emphatic doubling of ⲱⲣⲉϩ (= Sah. ⲱⲣϫ̄/ⲱⲣϩ 'guard, watch over'). The First Man's commission is to guard the five storehouses (= the five sons / five elements of light) descending into the Darkness.
Greek loanword ταμεῖον 'storehouse, chamber.' Refers here to the Five Storehouses = the Five Light Elements (ether, air, light, water, fire) which the First Man bears as armor into the abyss.

Translated 'his tree' throughout (ϣⲛⲉ = ϣⲏⲛⲉ 'tree'). Each of the four faces has a characteristic 'tree' in the Manichaean cosmological-correspondence schema: First Man's tree extends over the sons of darkness; Ambassador's tree is his image of light; Jesus' tree is his Wisdom of Light. Alternative reading 'garden' (ϣⲛⲏ) is possible but 'tree' fits the well-attested Manichaean tree-symbolism.

Translated 'his stature' (= ϭⲁⲓ̈ 'figure, stature, tall one'). Each face's ⲭⲁⲓ̈ is his bodily/cosmic extent: First Man's stature = his four sons riding on his body; Ambassador's stature of light = the cosmos; Jesus' stature = his holy Church. The translation preserves the bodily-figural sense.

Rendered 'Third Ambassador' — the standard Manichaean title (tertius legatus / πρεσβευτής τρίτος). Note that this entity is here designated 'the second face' even though his epithet contains 'Third'; the apparent paradox shows that 'Third Ambassador' has become a fixed title detached from any current ordinal position.
Translated 'the abyss.' Likely Lycopolitan ϣⲓⲕ 'pit, depth' with -ϩ suffix; refers to the lower realm into which the Third Ambassador's image is revealed in order to draw forth the captive light.
Translated 'to send forth.' Appears to be Lycopolitan causative ⲁ-ϩⲟⲱⲣⲟ from a verb of sending/dispatching. Used here of the Ambassador sending light upward and Wisdom sending souls.
Greek loanword αἰχμαλωτίζω 'take captive.' The feminine subject (ⲁⲥⲣ̄-) likely refers to the cosmos or to Matter which has captured the souls.

Tentatively translated 'his ship.' The form ϫⲁⲓ̈ ('ship, vessel, barque') here functions as a third correspondence-noun alongside ϣⲛⲉ and ⲭⲁⲓ̈. In Manichaean cosmology the Ambassador's ⲭⲁⲓ̈ is the cosmos itself, of which the ships of light (sun and moon) are the visible vehicles; ϫⲁⲓ̈ may pick up that nautical sense. Alternative: ⲟⲩϫⲁⲓ̈ 'salvation.'
Translated 'souls' (plural of ⲯⲩⲭⲏ in Lycopolitan). The Wisdom of Light sends to the souls so that they may come to her — the upward soteriological movement central to Manichaean salvation.
'The Error of the cosmos, the law of Sin' — paired cosmic principles personified, characteristic Manichaean diction. ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ and ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ both capitalized as cosmic agents.

Translated 'the Great Counsel' (ⲥⲁϫⲛⲉ = Sah. ϣⲟϫⲛⲉ 'counsel, deliberation'). This is the fourth face. Could refer to the Light Mind, the Mother of Life, or the Living Spirit — without further context the title is left as 'the Great Counsel.' The verbal-abstract sense ('counsel') is preferred over the agent ('counselor') unless the surviving lines clarify.

Translated 'the encompassing-circuit.' ⲕⲱⲧⲉ = 'circuit, surrounding region' — distinct from ⲕⲱⲧϩ 'pluck' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). Refers to the cosmic surrounding-zone within which the Great Counsel dwells.
